## b

*n.* 1. **硼** — a trivalent metalloid element; occurs both in a hard black crystal and in the form of a yellow or brown powder
2. **貝** — a logarithmic unit of sound intensity equal to 10 decibels
3. **靶** — (physics) a unit of nuclear cross section; the effective circular area that one particle presents to another as a target for an encounter
4. aerobic rod-shaped spore-producing bacterium; often occurring in chainlike formations; found primarily in soil
5. originally thought to be a single vitamin but now separated into several B vitamins
6. the 2nd letter of the Roman alphabet

## babble

## baby

*n.* 1. **娃娃, 嬰兒, 嬰幼兒, 孩兒, 寶寶** — a very young child (birth to 1 year) who has not yet begun to walk or talk
*“the baby began to cry again”*
*“she held the baby in her arms”*
2. the youngest member of a group (not necessarily young)
*“the baby of the family”*
*“the baby of the Supreme Court”*
3. an immature childish person
*“he remained a child in practical matters as long as he lived”*
*“stop being a baby!”*
4. an unborn child; a human fetus
*“I felt healthy and very feminine carrying the baby”*
*“it was great to feel my baby moving about inside”*
5. (slang) sometimes used as a term of address for attractive young women
6. a very young mammal
*“baby rabbits”*
*v.* 1. **姑息, 嬌養, 嬌縱, 寬縱, 放任** — treat with excessive indulgence
*“grandparents often pamper the children”*
*“Let's not mollycoddle our students!”*

*adj.* 1. **壞+的, 腐敗+的** — (of foodstuffs) not in an edible or usable condition
*“bad meat”*
*“a refrigerator full of spoilt food”*
2. **不可收回+的, 不可收集+的** — not capable of being collected
*“a bad (or uncollectible) debt”*
3. **劣+的, 差+的, 劣質+的** — below average in quality or performance
*“a bad chess player”*
*“a bad recital”*
4. **壞+的, 差+的** — nonstandard
*“so-called bad grammar”*
5. **不安全+的, 擔風險+的, 有風險+的** — not financially safe or secure
*“a bad investment”*
*“high risk investments”*
6. **不良, 壞, 不道德+的, 邪惡+的** — characterized by wickedness or immorality
*“led a very bad life”*
*adv.* 1. with great intensity (`bad' is a nonstandard variant for `badly')
*“the injury hurt badly”*
*“the buildings were badly shaken”*
2. very much; strongly
*“I wanted it badly enough to work hard for it”*
*“the cables had sagged badly”*

## bang

**發音：** /ˈbæŋ/
*n.* 1. **轟隆聲** — a sudden very loud noise

4. a vigorous blow
*“the sudden knock floored him”*
*“he took a bash right in his face”*
5. a border of hair that is cut short and hangs across the forehead
6. the swift release of a store of affective force
*“they got a great bang out of it”*
*“what a boot!”*
*v.* 1. **猛力關上, 甩, 甩上, 砰然關上** — close violently
*“He slammed the door shut”*
2. **發出砰的一聲, 砰砰作響** — move noisily
*“The window banged shut”*
*“The old man banged around the house”*
3. *(ambitransitive, slang, vulgar)* **幹 /幹** — To engage in sexual intercourse.
4. strike violently
*“slam the ball”*
5. to produce a sharp often metallic explosive or percussive sound
*“One of them banged the sash of the window nearest my bed”*
6. have sexual intercourse with
*“This student sleeps with everyone in her dorm”*
*“Adam knew Eve”*
*adv.* 1. directly
*“he ran bang into the pole”*
*“ran slap into her”*
*interj.* 1. **砰** — A sudden percussive sound, such as made by the firing of a gun, slamming of a door, etc.

**發音：** /ˈbɑːɡən/
*n.* 1. **買賣, 買賣合同, 成交協議, 成交條件, 交易** — an agreement between parties (usually arrived at after discussion) fixing obligations of each
*“he made a bargain with the devil”*
*“he rose to prominence through a series of shady deals”*
2. **契約 /契約, 合同** — An agreement between parties concerning the sale of property; or a contract by which one party binds themself to transfer the right to some property for a consideration, and the other party binds themself to receive the property and pay the consideration.
3. **便宜貨, 廉價貨, 特價商品** — an advantageous purchase
*“she got a bargain at the auction”*
*“the stock was a real buy at that price”*
4. **便宜貨 /便宜貨, 廉價品 /廉價品** — An item purchased for significantly less than the usual, or recommended, price
*v.* 1. **還價, 討價還價, 議價** — negotiate the terms of an exchange
*“We bargained for a beautiful rug in the bazaar”*
2. *(intransitive)* **議價 /議價, 侃價 /侃價, 砍價** — To make a bargain; to make a deal or contract for the exchange of property or services; to negotiate; to haggle.
3. come to terms; arrive at an agreement

<a id="entry-b-000855"></a>
## bargain down

*v.* 1. **議價, 殺價** — persuade the seller to accept a lower price
*“She beat the merchant down $100”*

<a id="entry-b-000856"></a>

*n.* 1. **買賣約定者, 商人** — someone who purchases and maintains an inventory of goods to be sold

## be

**發音：** /ˈbiː/
*v.* 1. **有, 是** — have the quality of being; (copula, used with an adjective or a predicate noun)
*“John is rich”*
*“This is not a good answer”*
2. **是, 有** — be identical to; be someone or something
*“The president of the company is John Smith”*
*“This is my house”*
3. **在, 有** — occupy a certain position or area; be somewhere
*“Where is my umbrella?" "The toolshed is in the back”*
*“What is behind this behavior?”*
4. **存在, 是, 有** — have an existence, be extant
*“Is there a God?”*
5. **舉行, 發生, 有** — happen, occur, take place
*“I lost my wallet; this was during the visit to my parents' house"”*
*“There were two hundred people at his funeral”*
6. **等於, 等同, 是** — be identical or equivalent to
*“One dollar equals 1,000 rubles these days!”*
*n.* 1. **邵, 鈹** — a light strong brittle grey toxic bivalent metallic element

*“Where do these books belong?”*

## better

**發音：** /ˈbɛt.ə/
*adj.* 1. *(comparative, form-of)* **更好, 比較好的 /比較好的, 較好的 /較好的** — comparative degree of good and well
2. (comparative of `good') superior to another (of the same class or set or kind) in excellence or quality or desirability or suitability; more highly skilled than another
*“You're a better man than I am, Gunga Din”*
*“a better coat”*
3. (comparative of `good') changed for the better in health or fitness
*“her health is better now”*
*“I feel better”*
4. (comparative and superlative of `well') wiser or more advantageous and hence advisable
*“it would be better to speak to him”*
*“the White House thought it best not to respond”*
5. more than half
*“argued for the better part of an hour”*
*adv.* 1. comparative of `well'; in a better or more excellent manner or more advantageously or attractively or to a greater degree etc.
*“She had never sung better”*
*“a deed better left undone”*
2. from a position of superiority or authority
*“father knows best”*
*“I know better.”*
*n.* 1. something superior in quality or condition or effect
*“a change for the better”*
2. someone who bets
3. a superior person having claim to precedence
*“the common man has been kept in his place by his betters”*
4. the superior one of two alternatives
*“chose the better of the two”*
*v.* 1. **使更好, 變好, 增進, 改善, 改正** — to make better
*“The editor improved the manuscript with his changes”*
2. surpass in excellence
*“She bettered her own record”*
*“break a record”*
3. get better
*“The weather improved toward evening”*

*n.* 1. **硬塊** — a solid piece of something (usually having flat rectangular sides)

<a id="entry-b-003854"></a>
## Boolean algebra

*n.* 1. **布爾代數 /布爾代數** — An algebraic structure (Σ,∨,∧,∼,0,1) where ∨ and ∧ are idempotent binary operators, ∼ is a unary involutory operator (called "complement"), and 0 and 1 are nullary operators (i.e., constants), such that (Σ,∨,0) is a commutative monoid, (Σ,∧,1) is a commutative monoid, ∧ and ∨ distribute with respect to each other, and such that combining two complementary elements through one binary operator yields the identity of the other binary operator. (See Boolean algebra (structure)#Axiomatics.)

## break

**發音：** /bɹeɪk/
*v.* 1. **使中止, 暫停, 結束, 終止, 中止** — terminate
*“She interrupted her pregnancy”*
*“break a lucky streak”*
2. **犯罪, 違法** — act in disregard of laws, rules, contracts, or promises
*“offend all laws of humanity”*
*“violate the basic laws or human civilization”*
3. **突然逃跑** — move away or escape suddenly
*“The horses broke from the stable”*
*“Three inmates broke jail”*
4. **破碎, 散去** — scatter or part
*“The clouds broke after the heavy downpour”*
5. **中止, 中斷, 停止, 打斷** — prevent completion
*“stop the project”*
*“break off the negotiations”*
6. **非法進入, 闖入** — enter someone's (virtual or real) property in an unauthorized manner, usually with the intent to steal or commit a violent act
*“Someone broke in while I was on vacation”*
*“They broke into my car and stole my radio!”*
*n.* 1. **弄破, 破壞, 弄壞** — the act of breaking something
*“the breakage was unavoidable”*
2. **休息** — An instance of breaking something into two or more pieces.
3. **暫停, 暫時的停頓, 中斷, 中止, 間歇** — a time interval during which there is a temporary cessation of something
4. **打破, 折斷, 破碎, 骨折, 破裂** — breaking of hard tissue such as bone
*“it was a nasty fracture”*
*“the break seems to have been caused by a fall”*
5. **打斷, 中斷, 中止** — an act of delaying or interrupting the continuity
*“it was presented without commercial breaks”*
*“there was a gap in his account”*
6. some abrupt occurrence that interrupts an ongoing activity
*“the telephone is an annoying interruption”*
*“there was a break in the action when a player was hurt”*

## but

*adv.* 1. **僅, 僅僅, 只不過, 只是, 只有** — and nothing more
*“I was merely asking”*
*“it is simply a matter of time”*
*conj.* 1. **可是, 但是, 不過 /不過** — However, although, nevertheless, on the other hand (introducing a clause contrary to prior belief or in contrast with the preceding clause or sentence).
2. **可是, 但是, 不過 /不過, 而** — On the contrary, rather (as a regular adversative conjunction, introducing a word or clause in contrast or contradiction with the preceding negative clause or sentence).
3. **除了……以外** — Except that (introducing a subordinate clause which qualifies a negative statement); also, (archaic) with omission of the subject of the subordinate clause, acting as a negative relative, "except one that", "except such that".
4. *(obsolete)* **只** — Only; solely; merely.

<a id="entry-b-005791"></a>
## byzant

*n.* 1. **古代羅馬金幣** — a gold coin of the Byzantine Empire; widely circulated in Europe in the Middle Ages

<a id="entry-b-005792"></a>
## byzantine

*n.* 1. a native or inhabitant of Byzantium or of the Byzantine Empire
*adj.* 1. **東正教+的** — of or relating to the Eastern Orthodox Church or the rites performed in it
*“Byzantine monks”*
*“Byzantine rites”*
2. **拜占庭+的** — of or relating to or characteristic of the Byzantine Empire or the ancient city of Byzantium
3. **複雜難懂+的, 費解+的, 複雜+的, 錯綜複雜+的** — highly complex or intricate and occasionally devious
*“the Byzantine tax structure”*
*“Byzantine methods for holding on to his chairmanship”*
